summary: Artemisia I of Caria (Ancient Greek Ἀρτεμισία; fl. 480 BCE) was queen of Halicarnassus and nearby islands within the Achaemenid satrapy of Caria. She fought as an ally of Xerxes I in the second Persian invasion of Greece, commanded ships at Artemisium and Salamis, and is praised by Herodotus — himself a Halicarnassian — for courage and counsel.
attribution: Adapted from Wikipedia, "Artemisia I of Caria" · CC BY-SA 4.0
etymology: Greek Ἀρτεμισία, related to the goddess Artemis; she belongs to the Lygdamid dynasty of Halicarnassus.
cultCenters: Delphi (Pausanias saw her statue among Persian figures)

sections.heading: Queen and admiral
paragraphs: Daughter of Lygdamis I by a Cretan mother, she takes the throne after her husband's death while their son Pisindelis is still young. Voluntarily she joins Xerxes' armament with five ships reputed second only to Sidon's; Herodotus marvels that a woman went of her own high-hearted valour.

Before Salamis she alone advises against a naval battle. In the fighting, pursued by an Athenian ship, she rams a friendly Calyndian vessel; the Athenians break off, thinking her a Greek or deserter, while Xerxes — mistaking the victim for an enemy — praises her as men becoming women and women men.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: The atlas id artemisia-halicarnassus is Artemisia I, the Salamis commander. Later Carian queens of the same name (notably Artemisia II, Mausolus' widow) are distinct historical figures.
